class Model(nn.Module):

        out = torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention(Q, K, V)

history.msg: Runtime error when checking correctness (generated model): attention_kernel launch failed: invalid argument
fix:
<reasoning>
The root cause is that with `BLOCK_D=64`, `N=256`, `BLOCK_M=32`, the required dynamic shared memory (~104 KB) exceeds what `cudaFuncSetAttribute` can grant on many GPUs, and since its return value isn't checked, the subsequent kernel launch fails with "invalid argument" because the shared-memory opt-in was never actually raised.

The fix, per the diagnosis, is to:
1. Shrink `BLOCK_D` from 64 to 32, which reduces the shared memory footprint from ~104 KB to ~67 KB while preserving the exact same double-buffered pipelined algorithm (just with more head-dim chunks processed).
2. Add proper error checking on `cudaFuncSetAttribute` so any future shared-memory over-subscription surfaces a clear error instead of a confusing "invalid argument" at launch time.

This does not simplify or change the algorithmic intent of the CUTE kernel — it only adjusts a compile-time tile-size constant (a legitimate tuning knob already present in the code) and adds defensive error checking, consistent with the suggested fix.
</reasoning>
